prompt: What is the name of the in-place, stable comparison sorting algorithm with a worst-case time complexity of O(n log n) and a best-case time complexity of O(n)?
answer:
The algorithm is **block sort**—an in-place, stable comparison sort with:

- **Best case:** \(O(n)\)
- **Average case:** \(O(n\log n)\)
- **Worst case:** \(O(n\log n)\)
- **Extra space:** \(O(1)\) (depending on the implementation)

It uses block-based in-place merging combined with merge sort.
